thehub_rescan.coverage: 86 routes, 602 page loads, Chromium, every route answered and rendered at every width.
thehub_rescan.contrast: Routes failing went from 86 to 1; distinct failing elements from 26 to 1. thehub-pr#432 removed the Hub's own sidebar, which held them.
thehub_rescan.unchanged: Unnamed buttons (8 elements on 12 routes) and unfocusable scroll regions (3 elements on 3 routes) are the same before and after.

horizontal_overflow.reading: The 12px overflow on six routes at 1280px is gone. Seven routes now overflow at 768px (/crossover and the six /ovnis tabs), where none did before. Overflow at 320 to 430px is unchanged. The new 768px overflow appeared between the two commits; which change caused it is not established here.

hypothesis_check.stated_before_the_rescan: TheHub's contrast failures drop sharply after #432.

pilot_recommendation.why: Its evidence is on current main. It has 18 distinct failing elements in 10 style signatures, and three of them fail on all 22 routes (the unnamed mobile menu button and the scrolling status strip), so a small change is verifiable on every route. It pins release 0.3.0, so the pilot also exercises moving a pin, which every other producer will need.
pilot_recommendation.why_second: The largest gain: 222 distinct contrast elements on 19 of 20 routes. They fall into 57 style signatures and 32 colour pairs, so it is a larger and more repetitive change, better done after the adoption path is proven once.

not_recommended_first.thehub-pr: After #432 it has 12 distinct failing elements left and a new 768px overflow that should be understood first.
not_recommended_first.spiderweb-pr: Its frontend changed on main since the evidence was taken, and it has one addressable route.
not_recommended_first.mucaro-ai, ovnis-pr: One addressable route each; the scan says little about them.

pilot_recommendation.decision_needed: The pilot application is the user's choice.
pilot_recommendation.status: Skywatcher, AguaYLuz, MoneySweep and Centinelas measured; thehub-pr fixed, scan pending at the time of this record.

blocked: macOS Dock menu and app identity
why_not_pass: Four applications are fixed and measured in Chromium by the author; a fifth, thehub-pr, is fixed and its scan is recorded separately. Pages were loaded, not operated; no keyboard walk-through, screen reader or touch device was used; Firefox and WebKit were not run against the applications; no change is merged; nobody independent has reviewed them.

pilot.scope: App-local fixes only, as chosen: no shared-package release, no pin move.
pilot.coverage: 22 routes at 7 widths, 154 page loads, before and after. Four sign-in routes redirect to / by design, before and after.
pilot.not_fixed: link-in-text-block: 13 page loads on 2 routes, unchanged. It was not in the pilot's scope.
pilot.no_regression_observed: Horizontal overflow 0 before and after; page errors 0; console errors 0; controls under 24px unchanged (870 summed over page loads).
changes: Mobile navigation toggle: accessible name that follows state, aria-expanded, 44px target.
lib/scrollRegion.js applied to every app-authored scrolling container (32 places), not only the 10 the scan caught.
Sky Target Finder rows: the button holds only the target name; the detail line is its description; click area unchanged.
pilot.tests: 141 unit tests pass (9 new), eslint clean, GUI parity ratchet passes, 26 of 26 CI checks on head 1301570.
corrections_during_the_pilot: Dropping the target buttons' aria-label broke seven existing tests that rely on the exact name; the row was restructured instead.
The first restructure left the name button 20px tall; the scan counted it under the 24px minimum and it was raised to 24px. Rows are 4px taller.
One parity-baseline entry was updated because the toggle's fingerprint changed; a full baseline regeneration was tried and reverted as too broad.
pilot.deviation_from_plan: The plan said the Sky Target Finder change would have no visible effect; rows are 4px taller. The plan named a ScrollRegion component; a ref helper was used so only opening tags change.

user_decisions: Raise the failing dim text to slate-400.
Fix all scanned failures, not contrast only.
second_application.coverage: 20 routes at 7 widths, 140 page loads, before and after. No route redirects.
second_application.not_fixed: link-in-text-block (14 page loads on 3 routes) and svg-img-alt (7 page loads on 1 route), both unchanged. Neither was in scope.
second_application.no_regression_observed: Horizontal overflow 0 before and after; page errors 0; controls under 24px unchanged (4096 summed over page loads); console errors on 7 page loads before and after.
changes: 312 uses of text-slate-500/600/700 in 40 files now use text-slate-400; a test keeps the failing shades from returning as text colours.
Selected range button: sky-600 to sky-700, plus aria-pressed.
Six unnamed filter select boxes named (the scan saw one; the other five had the same defect).
lib/scrollRegion.js applied to all 44 app-authored scrolling containers.
second_application.visible_change: Dim text is the same grey as muted text across the app. rc4/aguayluz_water_use_before_after.png shows one page, before above and after below.
second_application.tests: 277 unit tests pass, eslint clean, GUI parity ratchet passes, three Python test files that read the dashboard source pass.
second_application.ci: Not fully green. On the code head c60587e, 24 checks passed and 4 were cancelled by the next push. On the following head 9131d38 (a test-stub change), 24 passed and one job, certify-source-product-denominators, failed with a DNS resolution error while fetching a remote source; that job passed on the two previous heads. It has not been re-run.
second_application.limits: The scan ran on a workspace with little data on most pages. Text that appears only with data is covered by the class replacement and its test, not by the scan.
second_application.deviation_from_plan: The helper was not copied unchanged: it gained an optional second argument for an element that already has a ref. One parity-baseline entry was updated because a control's class changed. A code-scanning note about the helper led to a change in an unrelated test's ResizeObserver stub.
